item.title: Ebola: Keyamo directs airlines to bar 46 persons linked to outbreak from flying
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Wednesday, directed aviation authorities to place 46 persons who had contact with the Ebola-infected person on a no-fly list for 21 days to prevent the possible spread of the virus. Keyamo, who also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports, said he had instructed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to immediately inform all local and international airlines about the development. He disclosed this on X, formerly Twitter, after holding a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate. The minister stated: “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge. He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest). “I have therefore directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development. I have also directed FAAN to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports. Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” Vanguard News The post Ebola: Keyamo directs airlines to bar 46 persons linked to outbreak from flying appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Governor Yusuf assures
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has assured President Bola Tinubu of the support of the people of Kano State in the 2027 general election. According to him, the people of Kano will vote for the President to ensure the continuation of his development projects. Yusuf stated this on Wednesday while representing president Tinubu at the commissioning of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway at Tamburawa in Kano State. He praised the President for projects being executed by the Federal Government, saying that the highway would ease transportation across Northern Nigeria. Governor Yusuf also revealed that many projects executed by President Tinubu had not received adequate publicity. “I have seen many projects the President has executed that have not been publicised. I could go on and on listing the projects and initiatives of this administration,” Yusuf said. He expressed confidence that the people of Kano and other parts of the country would support Tinubu in the next general election. “The people of Kano will come out en masse to vote for President Tinubu, not only in Kano but across the North-West, the South and the country at large, to ensure the continuation of his development projects,” he added. Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the worst of Nigeria’s economic hardship was over. He insisted that Tinubu’s reforms were beginning to yield positive results. “The reforms have started to yield dividends of democracy. Even in the darkest hour before dawn, there is hope. Let us support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He cited road projects in Kano and other parts of the North-West as evidence of the administration’s efforts. He added that the Federal Government was working to complete projects inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “There is no project started by the late President Buhari that President Bola Tinubu is not doing in the North,” he said. Umahi listed several road projects in the region, including the Kano Northern Bypass, Kano Ring Road, Kano-Kongolam road project and the Zari-Hunkuyi road project. He also said the Federal Government was working on the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road. He added that some inherited projects had been redesigned to feature reinforced concrete pavement. According to Umahi, the Tinubu administration has completed close to 400 kilometres of roads in the North-West within three years, while about 4,000 kilometres of road projects are ongoing in the region. He said the Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Highway would benefit not only the North-West but also other parts of the country. item.title: Rice Rescues Arsenal In Champions League Tie Against Bayern Munich
item.description: Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season’s runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane. Kane put Bayern on track for victory when he converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point. The Gunners have seven points from three games in the league phase, two more than Bayern. Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout. “We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game,” Kane told DAZN. “Probably a draw was a fair result overall… There’s a lot of games and we’ve got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on.” Despite the absences, the England captain ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in Kane’s hometown of London. Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. item.title: Real Madrid Rout Leipzig, Continue Perfect European Start
item.description: Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goals for Jose Mourinho’s side. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval. Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on. Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona. Without a major trophy for two seasons and having endured a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form. The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP) Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso. Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a save at full stretch from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt. item.title: 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru
item.description: The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has described Northern Nigeria as the ruling party’s stronghold ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that both the region’s political elite and ordinary citizens support the party. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the North, citing the support of prominent political figures and the establishment of a campaign office known as Arewa for Asiwaju. “The strength of the APC is in the Northern part of this country and you will see it by the grace of God when election comes in 2027. On Saturday, we had the leading lights in politics, in economy, in industry gathering together to donate a campaign office they call Arewa for Asiwaju. “Even some who are in the opposition party have changed, people like the former governor of Niger State Babangida Aliyu, now all of them are coming to join and work for the APC. The truth is that today, when you see the creme de la creme of Northern Nigeria, they are with us, you see the masses of Northern Nigeria are with us,” Basiru said. ﻿ The APC National Secretary also criticised opposition parties over their response to electoral defeats, saying they should learn to accept losses as part of the democratic process. The first reported incident in April affected about 40 students, while more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure in May. Another 69 students were reportedly hospitalised on June 1 after another occurrence. Schools affected in previous incidents included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin, among others. The repeated incidents have raised concerns about the safety of students and staff, particularly as the emissions appear to recur in some of the same locations. Following previous incidents, Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, said the state government was working with relevant agencies and experts to determine the cause of the emissions. The governor said the Ministries of Environment and Health were collaborating with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority and the Department of Geology at Olabisi Onabanjo University to investigate the phenomenon. Abiodun, speaking on the matter in June, said gas analysers had been installed in affected schools following earlier incidents to determine the nature and concentration of the emissions. “Twice now, we have recorded cases of pollution in this school and some neighbouring schools. What is interesting is that the gas pollution occurred at about the same time in the affected schools—about three schools altogether—and this has happened on two separate occasions,” the governor said. He added: “Following the first occurrence, we installed gas analysers across the schools to determine the nature and concentration of the gas, which has now been confirmed to be methane.” The governor said preliminary findings pointed to possible geological factors, including fault lines, as a potential explanation for the emissions. “Preliminary findings suggest there may be geological factors involved, possibly fault lines common to these locations, which could be responsible for the emissions. We are awaiting the final report from the professionals handling the investigation,” he said. When contacted on Wednesday, the Ogun State Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said the government was monitoring the situation. “We are on top of the situation,” he said. Also speaking on the latest incident, Kehinde Bello, a Senior Special Assistant to Governor Abiodun and General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, said the emissions were linked to underground gas occurrences previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April 2026. Bello, who visited the affected areas in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo to assess the situation, said the government was working towards finding a lasting solution. He said investigations by the government had indicated that the phenomenon could be a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. However, the precise source of the emissions and the circumstances surrounding their repeated occurrence remain central concerns for residents of the affected communities. As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were reportedly attending to the affected students at the general hospitals and other healthcare facilities. The latest incident has intensified calls for a conclusive investigation and effective measures to prevent further exposure, particularly in schools, where students and staff remain vulnerable to the recurring emissions. item.title: Osimhen scores as Galatasaray defeat Lille 4-2 in Champions League thriller
item.description: Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen scored a crucial second-half goal as Galatasaray came from behind to defeat Lille 4-2 in the UEFA Champions League league phase on Wednesday. The Turkish champions recovered from a first-half deficit to secure all three points in an entertaining encounter in France, with six goals scored by both sides. Galatasaray took the lead in the second minute through Yunus Akgün, who converted a rebound from close range after Baris Yilmaz’s cross caused problems in the Lille penalty area. Lille responded five minutes later as Soriba Diaoune equalised in the seventh minute. The forward received a pass from Alexsandro, drove into the box and fired past Galatasaray goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir. The French side continued to threaten and took the lead in the 39th minute when Diaoune scored his second goal of the evening. Assisted by Hakon Arnar Haraldsson, he found space inside the penalty area before sending a first-time effort into the top-right corner. However, Galatasaray restored parity just before the break. Alexey Batrakov rose unmarked to head home Roland Sallai’s delivery in the 44th minute, ensuring both teams went into half-time level at 2-2. The visitors moved ahead again in the 52nd minute when Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer inadvertently turned the ball into his own net. Osimhen extended Galatasaray’s lead nine minutes later, finishing a swift counterattack with a first-time shot from mid-range after receiving a pass from Yilmaz. The goal made it 4-2 and gave Galatasaray a comfortable advantage as they sought to see out the contest. The Nigerian forward had earlier missed a promising opportunity in the 20th minute, while another effort was ruled out for offside in the 69th minute. However, his second-half strike proved decisive in the visitors’ victory. Lille attempted to mount a comeback, bringing on experienced striker Olivier Giroud and making further substitutions in search of goals. Galatasaray, however, remained organised defensively, with Cakir making important saves to frustrate the hosts. Despite late pressure, including a volley from Maurits Kjaergaard that narrowly missed the target, Lille could not find another goal as Galatasaray held on for a 4-2 victory. The result gave the Turkish side a significant boost in their Champions League campaign, while Osimhen’s goal underlined his importance to the team’s attacking threat. item.title: Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has said the wisdom and moral clarity of the late Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti will be greatly missed in Nigeria’s political landscape. Fasoranti, an elder statesman and leader of the Yoruba socio-political group, Afenifere, died at the age of 100. In a tribute, Tunji-Ojo said he joined the nation in mourning the late statesman with a heavy heart, describing his death as a significant loss to the country. “In him, Nigeria has lost a true leader and an enduring symbol of our democratic journey,” the minister said. He described Fasoranti’s century-long life as one anchored on selfless service, adding that his legacy stood as a testament to principled leadership. According to Tunji-Ojo, the late elder statesman was a lifelong disciple of the sage, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, and a longstanding leader of Afenifere. He said Fasoranti remained steadfast in his advocacy for justice, true federalism and the dignity of the Yoruba people, while also upholding national unity and democratic values. The minister said the late Afenifere leader’s contributions to the political evolution of Ondo State and Nigeria would remain indelible. He recalled that Fasoranti was recently celebrated in Lagos on attaining the age of 100, describing the occasion as a rare honour that reflected the respect he commanded across generations and political divides. “Only recently, we gathered in Lagos to celebrate him as a centenarian; a rare honour that underscored the depth of respect he commanded across generations and political divides. That celebration of a life well lived now turns to solemn reflection,” he said. Tunji-Ojo extended his condolences to the Fasoranti family, the people of Ondo State, members of Afenifere and all those inspired by the late elder statesman’s life. “May the Almighty grant his soul eternal rest and comfort those he left behind. Adieu, Pa Fasoranti. Your legacy of courage, service, and integrity endures,” the minister said. The post Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: Edo urges calm, compliance with safety guidelines
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Edo State Government has urged residents to remain calm and comply with public health guidelines following reports of a confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Cyril Oshiomhole, made the call on Wednesday during a press briefing on the reported case. Represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health, Dr Eighemherio Ikhumosa, Oshiomhole said the state government was monitoring developments in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). He described the development as a serious public health concern, adding that the ministry was engaging relevant health agencies and partners to strengthen preparedness and response measures. The commissioner advised residents to avoid contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons, wash their hands regularly with soap and water, and use appropriate alcohol-based hand sanitisers. He also warned against handling the personal belongings of confirmed cases without proper protective measures. Oshiomhole urged anyone who developed symptoms such as fever, weakness, headache or muscle pain, particularly after possible exposure to the virus, to seek immediate medical attention and follow the guidance of health professionals. He further cautioned residents against spreading unverified information that could cause unnecessary panic or undermine public health efforts. The commissioner urged the public to remain vigilant, stay calm and adhere to preventive measures as health authorities monitor the situation. item.title: Ebola Scare: NEMA DG urges calm, warns against contact with suspected cases

Umar warned against panic, misinformation and stigmatisation, saying the patient had been isolated and was receiving medical care, while contact tracing and surveillance continued. In a public advisory, the NEMA chief called for increased public awareness and cooperation with health officials, stressing that early detection and responsible behaviour were critical to preventing further transmission. She said the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), in collaboration with the FCT Health Services Secretariat and other relevant agencies, were leading the response. According to her, NEMA remained prepared to provide coordination and emergency support within the country’s emergency management framework as required. “Our most important message to Nigerians is: remain calm, remain vigilant and follow official health advice. There is no need for panic,” she said. item.title: Foreigners now seek Nigerian passports, Dabiri-Erewa says
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Director of Diaspora Mobilisation for the PBAT/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Abike Dabiri-Erewa, has said that an increasing number of foreign nationals are seeking Nigerian passports and expressing interest in staying in the country. Dabiri-Erewa disclosed this on Wednesday during a press briefing in Abuja, where she outlined the council’s plans to mobilise Nigerians in the diaspora in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. Speaking on the reported interest of foreigners in acquiring Nigerian citizenship, she said her office had received numerous appeals from non-Nigerians seeking assistance in obtaining Nigerian passports. “On my table, you see a lot of people telling us to beg the President to be able to give them Nigerian passports. Ask the Minister of Interior. It’s too much,” she said. She said the development reflected growing interest in Nigeria among some foreign nationals, including those seeking to invest in the country and establish closer ties with it. Dabiri-Erewa cited the example of a woman who recently told her team on camera that she had come to Nigeria and did not intend to return to her previous country of residence. She also highlighted the contributions of Nigerians living abroad, describing them as important stakeholders in the country’s development. According to her, Nigerians in the diaspora include doctors, nurses, engineers, students, traders, innovators and community leaders who contribute to the economy through remittances, investments and other forms of engagement. She said diaspora remittances exceeded $20 billion annually, adding that Nigerians abroad were also investing in sectors such as healthcare, education, agriculture and information and communications technology.
